Section 5 • \(\xi\)1D

5.1 Per-sample (realization-level) 1D two-point correlation

Given one realization \(s\) and a fixed sightline labelled by \(\vec{x}_{\perp}\), consider the fractional fluctuation fields \(\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\) and \(\delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\) associated with two transitions (or species-transition pairs) \(i\) and \(j\). The per-sample 1D two-point (cross) correlation function (2PCF) is then defined as an average along the available 1D spectral domain of that sightline.

For a finite spectral interval \([\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]\) of length \(L_\Lambda \coloneqq \Lambda_b-\Lambda_a\), we define (without periodic wrap)2 : \begin{align} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) &\equiv\; \left\langle \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) ,\; \delta_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) \right\rangle_{\Delta} \;\equiv\; \frac{1}{L-\Delta} \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b-\Delta}\! d\Lambda\; \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\, \delta_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda+\Delta\right). \tag{5.2} \end{align} The normalization \(L-\Delta\) accounts for the fact that, for a given \(\Delta\), only the sub-interval \([\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b-\Delta]\) contains values of \(\Lambda\) such that both \(\Lambda\) and \(\Lambda+\Delta\) lie inside the available domain.

Equivalently, introducing an explicit window function \begin{equation} W_{\Delta}(\Lambda)\equiv \mathbf{1}_{[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b-\Delta]}(\Lambda), \tag{5.3} \end{equation} one may write \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) \equiv \frac{ \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b}\! d\Lambda\; W_{\Delta}(\Lambda)\, \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\, \delta_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda+\Delta\right) }{ \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b}\! d\Lambda\; W_{\Delta}(\Lambda) }, \qquad 0\le \Delta < L_\Lambda. \tag{5.4} \end{equation}

Autocorrelation and symmetry.

For \(i=j\), \(\widehat{\xi}_{ii}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta)\) is the per-sample autocorrelation of the fluctuation field \(\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\) along the spectral coordinate. For \(i\neq j\), one has the general identity (for real-valued fields): \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ji}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) = \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},-\Delta\right). \tag{5.5} \end{equation} A commonly used symmetrized cross-correlation definition, which is even in the lag, is: \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ij,\mathrm{sym}}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) \;\equiv\; \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) + \widehat{\xi}_{ji}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) = \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) + \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},-\Delta\right), \qquad \Delta\ge 0. \tag{5.6} \end{equation} One may optionally include an overall factor \(1/2\), depending on convention; here we keep the explicit sum.

2

We will also consider the following definition for the lag-dependent window average when dealing with a single function: \begin{equation} \left\langle Q(\Lambda)\right\rangle_{\Delta} \;\coloneqq\; \frac{1}{L_\Lambda-\Delta} \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b-\Delta}\! d\Lambda\; Q(\Lambda), \qquad 0\le \Delta < L_\Lambda. \tag{5.1} \end{equation}
